*Problem family · all seven past Midterm 2 exams · 2–15 points · [[4-sampling-and-reconstruction/17-ideal-analog-to-digital-conversion|Lecture 17]], [[4-sampling-and-reconstruction/18-ideal-digital-to-analog-conversion|Lecture 18]], [[4-sampling-and-reconstruction/19-aliasing|Lecture 19]]*

## What it looks like on the exam

- **A** Nyquist rate (Hz) or period: part (a) of most sampling problems, 2–3 points.
- **B** Sketch $X_d(\omega)$ at a given $T$, often at two rates: opens every A/D → $H_d$ → D/A problem.
- **C** Which $T$ or $\Omega_0$ fit given samples: 6–12 points.
- **D** What the ideal D/A returns.
- **E** One or two True/False items.

Exams write $x_c$, $X_c$, $T_N$ ($T_{NYQ}$) for Lecture 17's $x_a$, $X_a$, $\frac{1}{2B}$.

## The recipe

> [!recipe] Sampling in six steps
> $$
> X_d(\omega)=\frac1T\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty}X_a\!\left(\frac{\omega-2\pi n}{T}\right),\qquad\omega=\Omega T.
> $$
> 1. **Nyquist.** Highest frequency $\Omega_{\max}$: band edge or largest tone. Product of sinusoids: the sum; $x_c(at)$: times $a$; $\cdot\cos(\Omega_ct)$: plus $\Omega_c$. $B=\Omega_{\max}/2\pi$; rate $2B$ Hz; $T_N=\frac{1}{2B}=\frac{\pi}{\Omega_{\max}}$. Criterion $f_s\gt2B$.
> 2. **Sketch $X_d$.** Relabel $\Omega\to\Omega T$, height times $\frac1T$, copy every $2\pi$. Edge $\Omega_{\max}T$ below $\pi$: guard band; at $\pi$: copies touch; above: overlap.
> 3. **Add overlapping copies** as formulas in $\omega$. Opposite ramps give a constant; an odd spectrum can cancel. Label $\frac1T$, break points, $\pm\pi$. Check: period average $=x_c(0)$.
> 4. **Which $T$ or $\Omega_0$.** Plain cosine: $\Omega_0T\equiv\pm\omega_0\pmod{2\pi}$. Sine or phased cosine: $+\omega_0$ only. Solve $T=\frac{\omega_0+2\pi k}{\Omega_0}$ or $\Omega_0=\frac{\omega_0+2\pi k}{T}$; several tones: intersect.
> 5. **D/A of a sinusoid.** Fold $\Omega_0T$ into $(-\pi,\pi)$ to get $\hat\omega$; output at $\hat\Omega=\hat\omega/T$, i.e. $\hat f=f_0-kf_s$ with $\lvert\hat f\rvert\lt\frac{f_s}{2}$. Negative $\hat\Omega$ flips a sine's sign and a cosine's phase. Lecture 19: $\sin(100\pi t)$ at 80 Hz returns $-\sin(60\pi t)$.
> 6. **D/A of samples.** $x_a(t)=\sum_nx[n]\,\mathrm{sinc}\!\left(\frac{\pi(t-nT)}{T}\right)$, $\mathrm{sinc}(t)=\frac{\sin t}{t}$: one two-sided sinc per sample, never an impulse or a staircase.

> [!trap] Where the points go
> - **Strict or not.** Keys accept $T=\frac{1}{2B}$ for a sketched $X_c$ zero at its edge (FA2021 #5(a), FA2024 #5(a)), not for a sinusoid: $\sin(40\pi t)$ at $T=\frac{1}{40}$ is $\sin(\pi n)=0$ (SP2025 #6(b)).
> - **Missing $\frac1T$:** 5000, not 1 (SP2021 #8).
> - **Hz vs rad/s.** $1000\pi$ rad/s is 500 Hz: $T_N=1$ ms, not $\frac{1}{2000}$ s (FA2024 #5(a)).
> - **Sign flips.** $\Omega_0=-200\pi$ gives $-\sin(\frac{\pi}{2}n)$ (FA2023 #3); $f_s=55$ Hz fails SP2025 #6(c) on the sign alone.
> - **Modulo $2\pi$.** An aliasing $T$ can still fit: $T=\frac{1}{40}$ in SP2025 #6(a).

## Practice problems

> [!question] Practice 1 — a trapezoid at three rates
> $X_a(\Omega)=1$ for $\lvert\Omega\rvert\le100\pi$, falls linearly to 0 at $\lvert\Omega\rvert=300\pi$. Sketch $X_d$ on $[-\pi,\pi]$ for (a) $T=\frac{1}{400}$ s, (b) $T=\frac{1}{300}$ s, (c) $T=\frac{1}{240}$ s. (d) $x[0]$?

> [!success]- Solution
> $B=150$ Hz, $T_N=\frac{1}{300}$ s. Flat top ends at $100\pi T$, ramp at $300\pi T$, height $\frac1T$.
> **(a)** Height 400, flat to $\frac{\pi}{4}$, zero from $\frac{3\pi}{4}$; next copy from $\frac{5\pi}{4}$: guard band $\frac{\pi}{2}$.
> **(b)** Height 300, flat to $\frac{\pi}{3}$, zero at exactly $\pi$: copies touch.
> **(c)** Height 240, flat to $\frac{5\pi}{12}$; the ramp ends at $\frac{5\pi}{4}$, the next copy rises from $\frac{3\pi}{4}$; the two ramps add to $240\cdot\frac{\pi/2}{5\pi/6}=144$:
> $$
> X_d(\omega)=\begin{cases}240,&\lvert\omega\rvert\le\frac{5\pi}{12}\\[2pt]240\,\dfrac{5\pi/4-\lvert\omega\rvert}{5\pi/6},&\frac{5\pi}{12}\le\lvert\omega\rvert\le\frac{3\pi}{4}\\[2pt]144,&\frac{3\pi}{4}\le\lvert\omega\rvert\le\pi.\end{cases}
> $$
> **(d)** $x[0]=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int X_a\,d\Omega=\frac{400\pi}{2\pi}=200$ in every case.

> [!question] Practice 2 — which $T$ give $\cos(3\pi n/4)$?
> $\cos(60\pi t)$ is sampled to $\cos(\frac{3\pi}{4}n)$. (a) Every such $T$. (b) Which of $T=\frac{1}{80},\frac{1}{60},\frac{1}{48},\frac{1}{40},\frac{1}{16}$ s fit? (c) Repeat (b) for $\sin(60\pi t)\to\sin(\frac{3\pi}{4}n)$.

> [!success]- Solution
> **(a)** $60\pi T\equiv\pm\frac{3\pi}{4}$: $T=\frac{3+8k}{240}$ ($k\ge0$) or $\frac{8k-3}{240}$ ($k\ge1$): $\frac{1}{80},\frac{1}{48},\frac{11}{240},\frac{13}{240},\dots$
> **(b)** $\frac{1}{80}$: $\frac{3\pi}{4}$ ✓. $\frac{1}{48}$: $\frac{5\pi}{4}\equiv-\frac{3\pi}{4}$ ✓. $\frac{1}{60}$: $\pi$ ✗. $\frac{1}{40}$: $\equiv-\frac{\pi}{2}$ ✗. $\frac{1}{16}$: $\equiv-\frac{\pi}{4}$ ✗.
> **(c)** Sine: $+\frac{3\pi}{4}$ only. $\frac{1}{80}$ ✓; $\frac{1}{48}$ gives $-\sin(\frac{3\pi}{4}n)$ ✗.

> [!question] Practice 3 — what the ideal D/A gives back
> $x_a(t)=3\cos(240\pi t+\frac{\pi}{6})+\sin(60\pi t)$ through ideal A/D and D/A. (a) $y_a(t)$ at $f_s=200$ Hz? (b) Smallest $f_s$ with $y_a=x_a$? (c) Which $f_s$ in 100–240 Hz brings the 120 Hz term out at 40 Hz?

> [!success]- Solution
> **(a)** $\frac{240\pi}{200}=1.2\pi\equiv-0.8\pi$, $\hat\Omega=-160\pi$; the 30 Hz term ($0.3\pi$) is unaliased:
> $$
> y_a(t)=3\cos\!\left(160\pi t-\tfrac{\pi}{6}\right)+\sin(60\pi t).
> $$
> **(b)** $f_s\gt240$ Hz, strictly: at 240 Hz the first term samples to $\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}(-1)^n$.
> **(c)** $\lvert120-kf_s\rvert=40$, $40\lt\frac{f_s}{2}$: only $f_s=160$ Hz. $\frac{3\pi}{2}\equiv-\frac{\pi}{2}$, $\hat\Omega=-80\pi$: $3\cos(80\pi t-\frac{\pi}{6})$.
